name: tool-list
about: The one tool and its input schema.

answer.name: project-map
answer.description: Use this single Metaform tool for add, update, delete, orphaned, goto, map, raw dumps and addressed reads. Work on one receiving element at a time. Input addresses select actual elements in the nested namespace. wants records refer to providers at their own locations.

inputSchema.description: A command name (add, update, delete, orphaned, goto, map) is a command. A key that starts with a period is a raw dump. Any other key is an address, and reads that element. The selected project comes from caller context. Addresses in commands are selectors; storage remains a nested namespace.

oneOf.description: goto places the agent at an address and returns its summary sheet: the element and its wants, what relies on it, layer record counts, skill frontmatter and the memory count. A later goto to the same address in the same context returns only what changed.
map returns the shallow graph: every element address, each want as an edge from the element that holds it to the element it names, and the one Definitive element. No fields and no layers.

A key that starts with a period is a raw dump: the stored nested JSON at that path, which is the JSON path $.<project><path> with $.<project> left off. "." dumps the whole project; ".code.server" dumps that element and everything beneath it. Every layer is included.
An addressed read: the element's own fields, plus each layer named with {} as its value.

NamespaceValue.title: Value at a namespace address
NamespaceValue.description: Objects extend the addressed hierarchy or hold structured data. Arrays denote composed element layers; scalars are direct values.

NamespaceNode.title: Namespace branch or receiving element
NamespaceNode.description: Namespace branch or receiving element. Its properties and layers are directly on the element. The same word can name metadata or a namespace branch according to its value and context.

anyOf.description: The name used for this functionality in project documentation or specifications, such as Metaform.

Systemic role: Definitive (the element whose loss means the artifact can no longer remain what it is), Supportive (an indivisibly coupled element meant to assist the Definitive element), Notable (a discrete, structurally independent feature or specialized exception with unique systemic significance) or Divergent (an unaligned, weak or redundant element to be realigned or ejected).

Implementation state. Use un_built for intended functionality not yet built. Legacy missing/todo spellings and intake BKN/broken judgments are not accepted. Other lifecycle state names are not defined by this schema.

The well-understood practitioner short name derived from the leaf segments. Must exactly match the same number of leading words of the reversed, space-separated namespace address, and must not match `name`.

wants.description: An object keyed by provider addresses, each holding a want record, is the functional knowledge layer. Any other object is a namespace branch and follows namespace rules.

anyOf.description: Optional project metadata; does not introduce a required wrapper.
One source link to the entry point for this functionality. A relative file path is allowed.

providers.description: This word may name a namespace branch. The functional relationship array is wants, not providers.

propertyNames.description: One namespace segment, never a dotted reference or JSONPath expression.

ComposedElementLayer.title: Array-valued composed element layer
ComposedElementLayer.description: An array at an element is a knowledge layer. Its members retain their native formats and nesting. Do not reinterpret fields inside native members as functional namespace branches.

Wants.title: Functional knowledge layer
Wants.description: Relationships owned by this receiver, keyed by the provider's address: one relationship per provider. Each key refers to the actual provider in the nested tree. The provider keeps its properties and knowledge at its own location.

propertyNames.description: Project-relative reference to an element in the actual nested namespace.

WantRecord.title: Want record
WantRecord.description: Why this receiver wants this provider, what the provider supplies for that goal, and what the receiver plans to do with the substance. Keep one relationship per provider address within a receiver.

direction.description: The direction of the substantial flow of information which satisfies the (OP) goal, relative to the receiver, not including the request: outbound from the receiver, inbound to the receiver, or two-way.

why.description: What this receiver seeks to accomplish through this provider. This is its Operative Purpose (OP). Use clear, simple technical English.

how.description: How this provider serves this receiver's goal in this encounter. This is its Encounter Function (EF). Use clear, simple technical English.

LayerRead.description: Name each layer to read at the address where it is written, with {} as its value, such as {"wants": {}} or {"specification": {}}. An empty object reads only the element's own fields.

propertyNames.description: One layer name: one namespace segment.

AddFields.description: Fields supplied for one receiving element. Command addresses select actual nested elements.

WantsUpdate.description: Like Wants; each record holds only the fields to change.

propertyNames.description: One namespace segment, never a dotted reference or JSONPath expression.

UpdateFields.description: Update supplied fields on one receiving element. Null removes a property; omission leaves it unchanged. Delete individual wants with delete.

RelationshipWord.description: This word may name a namespace branch or native layer. Scalar relationship fields belong inside wants, not on the element.

specification.name: Specification
specification.description: Prose that the skeleton leaves out on purpose: what each element does, how it behaves and why, as blocks with Markdown heading levels.
specification.instruction:
Write each block in TASTE: Technically Accurate, Simple, Transparent English. A block adds what the map leaves out on purpose; do not repeat what the element's fields and wants already say.
- Start with what the element does or holds. Then give the detail that explains it.
- Name the element, field or command instead of starting with "it", "this" or "they". A block is often read alone.
- Use the project's terms and exact identifiers. Use one term for one thing. Put identifiers in backticks.
- Write one claim per sentence. Aim for 25 words or fewer per sentence and six sentences or fewer per paragraph. Never cut a condition, an exception or a reason to meet a length target.
- Use lowercase must, should, may, can and might with their TASTE meanings. Do not write SHALL or capitalized MUST.
- Say whether something is built, proposed or planned. Do not describe planned behavior as if it exists.
- Replace words such as simple, robust or fast with the behavior or a measurement.
- Define an abbreviation at its first use. Keep noun clusters to three nouns.
- Leave out openings such as "This section describes", repeated points, analogies and promotion.
- Prefer start, use, adjust, perform and end over kick off/launch/begin, utilize/leverage, modify/change/alter, execute/run and terminate/stop/abort, when the meaning stays the same.
- Do not put Markdown heading lines in the text. Set the block's level and title instead.

element.name: Specification
element.description: Prose that the skeleton leaves out on purpose: what each element does, how it behaves and why, as blocks with Markdown heading levels.

answer.guidance:
The specification field is a list of blocks: {"level": 1-4, "title": "...", "text": "..."}. A titled block may also carry "code", a key that other text can cite; it is unique in the layer across the map, ignoring case. The first block may be {"text": "..."} alone, as an intro under the element's heading. The first titled block is level 1, and each level is at most one more than the level before it. update replaces every block at the address and is safe to repeat; add appends blocks; if an answer is lost, a retried add appends them twice. Read them with {"<address>": {"specification": {}}}. The root's blocks are in the raw dump {".": {}}, because a key that starts with a period is a raw dump. Blocks are accepted at an element that has technical_name, name and role, and at . once the map has a Definitive element.
